articles.detail: 5 cycles ran and all 5 wrote articles (11/12/13/13/12); 2 committed and deployed themselves, 2 were swept into the manual dev-session commits, and the 22:00 batch of 12 is still uncommitted

experiment: Skipped — every goal metric is inside target, no experiment is active, and no pause gate applies. The day's failures are all in the build/deploy stage, which no tunable parameter in this scope touches; opening a variable now would only add noise to a day whose content numbers are already clean.
weakestArea: Deploy, not content. Three of five cycles reached Stage 3b and never shipped: 12:00 died with ENOTEMPTY inside build.js's rmSync of dist/, and 17:00 and 22:00 both found .build.lock held by a live PID and exited. The lock behaved exactly as designed — it was added on 2026-08-03 for this race and it prevented a second corrupted build — but the holder was a long-running local build from the map-engine work, so scheduled cycles queued behind an interactive session for ten hours. Of the content metrics, tech is softest: 9 articles against a floor of 4 is comfortable, but it fell from 14 yesterday and the 17:00 cycle logged a post-dedup floor violation (tech 2 < 3).
watching: The 22:00 cycle's 12 articles are written, validated and still untracked in content/articles/ — they are not on the live site until someone commits and runs a build; .build.lock is now clear, so a plain publish will take them.

The build lock has no wait or retry: run-cycle.sh treats a held lock as a build failure and skips deploy outright, so any concurrent local build silently costs a whole cycle's publication. Two cycles today, both recoverable only by hand.

The ENOTEMPTY at 12:00 is the same dist/ race the lock was written to stop, but it happened to the process that won the lock — a second writer was inside dist/ without holding it, which points at something other than build.js touching that tree.

Multi-source supply upstream stayed thin: 12:00 saw only 4 multi-source clusters and could not meet the economy floor at all (both economy clusters were the same 12 August eclipse). Published multi-source still landed at 9, so the selector is spending what little the feed gives it.
FIRMS_MAP_KEY is still absent from the service file — the thermal snapshot skipped on all five cycles and the map continues to serve a stale layer.
coverageGaps: Oceania produced a single article for the third consecutive day, and Africa at 5 remains the thinnest region with real output.
The Middle East took 17 of 55 slots (31%) — inside every stated target, but the widest single-region share this week.
Tech fell to 9 from 14 with the 17:00 cycle unable to fill its floor of 3; the shortfall was upstream feed composition, not selector behaviour.
acronymViol=379 in the 22:00 quality snapshot is far above the rest of the style panel and nothing currently gates it.
context: Content-side the day was healthy: 55 articles (up from 51), zero duplicates, 35 unique sources against 29 yesterday, freshness median 0.8 with a 1.5-day maximum, and no source above 15% share. Cycle wall-time averaged 1160s with the selector at 269s, writer 312s and editor 91s — all far inside their timeouts, and the writer's /tmp sandbox refusal did not recur after the --add-dir /tmp fix. The experiment slate is empty and the queued numerical-density experiment stays blocked on its own preflight (replicate the bench gain at n>=20 first); it targets scripts/write-prompt.md, which is outside daily-tuning scope in any case. Every failure today lives in scripts/build.js and scripts/run-cycle.sh, also outside that scope — the operator call worth making is whether a held build lock should make run-cycle.sh wait and retry rather than abandon the deploy.
